claim: The genetic code of Saccharomyces cerevisiae was sequenced 25 years ago.
source: Although the genetic code of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae was sequenced 25 years ago, the characterization of the roles of genes within it is far from complete.
evidence: References established scientific knowledge about the timing of yeast genome sequencing

claim: The characterization of the roles of genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae is far from complete.
source: Although the genetic code of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae was sequenced 25 years ago, the characterization of the roles of genes within it is far from complete.
evidence: Statement about the current state of gene function characterization

claim: Flow-injection time-of-flight mass spectrometry was used to dynamically profile the metabolome of 164 loss-of-function mutants.
source: Here, we used flow-injection time-of-flight mass spectrometry to dynamically profile the metabolome of 164 loss-of-function mutants in TOR and receptor or receptor-like genes under a time course of rapamycin treatment, generating a dataset with >7000 metabolomics measurements.
evidence: Direct description of the experimental method used in the study

claim: The study generated a dataset with more than 7000 metabolomics measurements.
source: Here, we used flow-injection time-of-flight mass spectrometry to dynamically profile the metabolome of 164 loss-of-function mutants in TOR and receptor or receptor-like genes under a time course of rapamycin treatment, generating a dataset with >7000 metabolomics measurements.
evidence: Quantitative description of the dataset size

claim: The data are made available through an interactive data visualization app hosted at https://rapamycin-yeast.ethz.ch.
source: In order to provide a resource to the broader community, those data are made available for browsing through an interactive data visualization app hosted at https://rapamycin-yeast.ethz.ch.
evidence: Statement about data availability and access

claim: Dynamic metabolite responses to rapamycin are more informative than steady-state responses when recovering known regulators of TOR signaling.
source: We demonstrate that dynamic metabolite responses to rapamycin are more informative than steady-state responses when recovering known regulators of TOR signaling, as well as identifying new ones.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparative analysis of dynamic vs steady-state measurements

claim: Deletion of a subset of novel genes causes phenotypes and proteome responses to rapamycin that implicate them in TOR signaling.
source: Deletion of a subset of the novel genes causes phenotypes and proteome responses to rapamycin that further implicate them in TOR signaling.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from phenotypic and proteomic analyses

claim: CFF1 is connected to the regulation of pyrimidine biosynthesis through URA10.
source: We found that one of these genes, CFF1, was connected to the regulation of pyrimidine biosynthesis through URA10.
evidence: Specific finding about CFF1's role in metabolic regulation

claim: The Saccharomyces cerevisiae genetic code was sequenced by Goffeau et al. in 1996.
source: Despite the long-standing sequencing of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae genetic code (Goffeau et al., 1996), the characterization of the roles of genes and proteins within it is an ongoing process (Wood et al., 2019).
evidence: Citation to the original genome sequencing publication

claim: The characterization of the roles of genes and proteins in Saccharomyces cerevisiae is an ongoing process.
source: Despite the long-standing sequencing of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae genetic code (Goffeau et al., 1996), the characterization of the roles of genes and proteins within it is an ongoing process (Wood et al., 2019).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to recent review

claim: Flow-injection analysis mass spectrometry can measure the metabolome profile of cells in less than a minute per sample.
source: With the advent of high-throughput metabolomics, including flow-injection analysis mass spectrometry (FIA-MS), it is possible to measure the metabolome profile of cells in less than a minute per sample (Fuhrer et al., 2011).
evidence: Statement about analytical method capabilities supported by citation

claim: Metabolomics has been used to uncover phenotypes for silent mutations.
source: For example, metabolomics has been used to uncover phenotypes for silent mutations (Raamsdonk et al., 2001).
evidence: Example of metabolomics application supported by citation

claim: High-throughput approaches have been used on a genome-wide scale to measure amounts of amino acids in yeast deletion mutants.
source: In the past, pioneering work has demonstrated that high-throughput approaches can be used on a genome-wide scale to measure amounts of amino acids in yeast deletion mutants for the purpose of characterizing regulatory principles of biosynthesis (Mülleder et al., 2016a).
evidence: Description of prior work supported by citation

claim: The target of rapamycin (TOR) signaling system is a core regulator of growth decisions in eukaryotic cells.
source: The target of rapamycin (TOR) signaling system is a core regulator of these decisions around growth in eukaryotic cells (reviewed in González and Hall, 2017).
evidence: Statement about TOR function supported by review citation

claim: Two functionally distinct sets of TOR protein complexes exist: TORC1 (sensitive to rapamycin) and TORC2 (not sensitive to rapamycin).
source: This includes the discovery of two functionally distinct sets of TOR protein complexes, one of which (TORC1) is sensitive to inhibition by rapamycin and a second complex (TORC2) which is not (reviewed in Eltschinger and Loewith, 2016).
evidence: Description of TOR complexes supported by review citation

claim: The study characterized the effects of 85 mutants in TOR-related signaling genes on the metabolome response to rapamycin.
source: Thus, we characterized the effects of a collection of 85 mutants in TOR-related signaling genes on the metabolome response of the cell to rapamycin (Figure 1A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Description of experimental design with reference to figure

claim: The mutant collection included deletions in regulators that act upstream of TORC1, as well as downstream kinases or genes involved TOR-related processes such as autophagy.
source: The mutant collection included deletions in regulators that act upstream of TORC1, as well as downstream kinases or genes involved TOR-related processes such as autophagy.
evidence: Description of the composition of the mutant collection

claim: Only nonessential mutants were selected for the collection.
source: Only nonessential mutants were selected for the collection.
evidence: Statement about selection criteria for mutants

claim: Cultures were grown to an optical density at 600 nm (OD600) of 0.7 before rapamycin treatment.
source: Cultures were grown to an optical density at 600 nm (OD600) of 0.7 at which point metabolites were extracted and a rapamycin treatment (400 ng/mL) was performed.
evidence: Description of experimental conditions

claim: Rapamycin treatment was performed at a concentration of 400 ng/mL.
source: Cultures were grown to an optical density at 600 nm (OD600) of 0.7 at which point metabolites were extracted and a rapamycin treatment (400 ng/mL) was performed.
evidence: Specification of rapamycin concentration used

claim: Rapamycin treatment inhibits TORC1 and elicits important dynamic responses in terms of metabolite levels and downstream signaling events.
source: Rapamycin treatment inhibits TORC1 and elicits important dynamic responses in terms of metabolite levels and downstream signaling events (Stracka et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement about rapamycin effects supported by citation

claim: Polar metabolite extracts were prepared after 5, 30, 60, and 90 min of rapamycin treatment.
source: We aimed to capture these dynamic effects in our mutant strains by preparing polar metabolite extracts after 5, 30, 60, and 90 min of rapamycin treatment.
evidence: Description of sampling time points

claim: The effect of rapamycin treatment on wild-type yeast measured by FIA-MS was validated by LC-MS.
source: The effect of rapamycin treatment on wild-type yeast as measured by high-throughput FIA-MS was orthogonally validated by a longer liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based measurement method (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Description of validation experiment with reference to figure

claim: TORC1 regulates amino acid and nucleotide metabolism.
source: TORC1 is known to regulate many metabolic functions, but amino acid and nucleotide metabolism exhibit characteristic changes when TORC1 is inactivated (Oliveira et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: Statement about TORC1 function supported by citations

claim: The levels of most amino acids increase after rapamycin treatment due to inhibition of translational initiation.
source: Specifically, the levels of most amino acids increase after rapamycin treatment due to inhibition of translational initiation (Berset et al., 1998), with some exceptions such as serine (Mülleder et al., 2016a; Oliveira et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement about metabolic response supported by citations

claim: Upon TORC1 inactivation through starvation, nucleotide degradation increases, leading to increased pool sizes of nucleoside-related compounds.
source: Upon TORC1 inactivation through starvation, nucleotide degradation increases, which leads to increased pool sizes of nucleoside-related compounds (Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: Statement about metabolic response supported by citation

claim: Changes in metabolite levels such as nucleosides were observed when wild-type yeast were treated with rapamycin.
source: Consistent with reports in the literature (Oliveira et al., 2015), changes in metabolite levels such as nucleosides were seen when wild-type yeast were treated with rapamycin (Figure 1B).
evidence: Observation from experimental data with reference to figure and citation

claim: The highest number of changes in metabolite levels across all mutants were observed after 90 min of rapamycin treatment.
source: The highest number of changes in metabolite levels across all mutants were observed after 90 min of rapamycin treatment (Figure 1D).
evidence: Observation from data analysis with reference to figure

claim: Treating cells with rapamycin can reveal metabolic responses that are not measurable prior to treatment.
source: These results show that treating the cells with rapamycin can reveal metabolic responses that are not measurable prior to treatment.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental observations

claim: Deleting genes that are positive upstream regulators of TOR signaling reduces the signal propagated through that system.
source: Deleting genes that are positive upstream regulators of TOR signaling reduces the signal propagated through that system (Péli-Gulli et al., 2015), and thus either causes changes in the metabolome that resemble those resulting from rapamycin treatment (Mülleder et al., 2016a) or could further sensitize the cell to TORC1 inhibition.
evidence: Statement about genetic effects supported by citations

claim: gtr1 is a mutant in a key positive regulator of TOR signaling that acts upstream of TORC1.
source: gtr1, a mutant in a key positive regulator of TOR signaling that acts upstream of TORC1 (Binda et al., 2009), showed elevated levels of glutamine compared with wild-type in the absence of rapamycin (Figure 1E).
evidence: Statement about gene function supported by citation and experimental observation

claim: gtr1 showed elevated levels of glutamine compared with wild-type in the absence of rapamycin.
source: gtr1, a mutant in a key positive regulator of TOR signaling that acts upstream of TORC1 (Binda et al., 2009), showed elevated levels of glutamine compared with wild-type in the absence of rapamycin (Figure 1E).
evidence: Experimental observation with reference to figure

claim: The gtr1 mutant showed a much stronger accumulation of phenylalanine than wild-type after rapamycin treatment.
source: However, the gtr1 mutant showed a much stronger accumulation of the amino acid than did wild-type after rapamycin treatment (Figure 1F).
evidence: Experimental observation with reference to figure

claim: Some metabolic alterations manifested by deleting genes involved in TOR signaling are only revealed after treatment with rapamycin.
source: Thus, some metabolic alterations manifested by deleting genes involved in TOR signaling are only revealed after treatment with rapamycin.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental observations

claim: The study assembled a collection of 85 receptor-related loss-of-function mutants.
source: Building on the investigation of known TOR signaling genes, we assembled another collection of 85 loss-of-function mutants. These mutants were selected for being known receptors, nutrient sensing proteins in S. cerevisiae, showing sequence similarity to known receptors in other species, or carrying protein domains that are common in receptor proteins (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Description of mutant collection assembly

claim: The empirical likelihood for the distances between positive regulators being as low as observed was calculated to be less than 5% for all time points tested.
source: Indeed, the empirical likelihood for the distances between positive regulators being as low as was observed was calculated to be <5% for all time points that were tested (Figure 2B).
evidence: Statistical analysis result with reference to figure

claim: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was greater than 0.5 for all time points.
source: When the area under a receiver operating characteristic curve was calculated for each time point, the values were >0.5 for all the time points (Figure 2BC).
evidence: Statistical analysis result with reference to figure

claim: The area under the curve for the untreated cells was the smallest of all the time points.
source: The area under the curve for the untreated cells was observed to be the smallest of all the time points, indicating that a dynamic perturbation by rapamycin treatment improved the recovery of true positives (Figure 2B).
evidence: Observation from analysis with reference to figure

claim: Dynamic perturbation by rapamycin treatment improved the recovery of true positives.
source: The area under the curve for the untreated cells was observed to be the smallest of all the time points, indicating that a dynamic perturbation by rapamycin treatment improved the recovery of true positives (Figure 2B).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from statistical analysis

claim: Small but significant correlations were seen between metabolome distances and genetic interaction scores.
source: However, when the metabolome distances between mutants were compared with the genetic interaction score between genes (Costanzo et al., 2016), small but significant correlations were seen between the datasets (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Result from comparative analysis with reference to figure and citation

claim: Six receptor-related mutants (RGT2, HXK2, URE2, BCK1, CLA4, and CFF1) were selected as potential novel positive regulators.
source: Six receptor-related mutants (RGT2, HXK2, URE2, BCK1, CLA4, and CFF1) were able to pass this cutoff and were selected as potential novel positive regulators (Figure 2DE).
evidence: Result from analysis with reference to figure

claim: RGT2 and HXK2 are involved in sugar sensing via the PKA signaling, which feeds into the regulation of downstream TORC1 signaling targets.
source: Namely, RGT2 and HXK2 are involved in sugar sensing via the PKA signaling, which feeds into the regulation of downstream TORC1 signaling targets (Shashkova et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement about gene function supported by citation

claim: URE2 is a transcriptional regulator for nitrogen catabolite repression, which is in part regulated by TORC1.
source: URE2 is a transcriptional regulator for nitrogen catabolite repression, which is in part regulated by TORC1 (Shashkova et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement about gene function supported by citation

claim: CFF1 has recently been named based on its inability to produce the compound 4-hydroxymethylfuranone.
source: The other hits included the intracellular kinases BCK1 and CLA4, as well as a gene of poorly characterized function YML079W, which has recently been named CFF1 based on its inability to produce the compound 4-hydroxymethylfuranone (Valastyan et al., 2021).
evidence: Statement about gene naming supported by citation

claim: atg13 is incapable of performing autophagy.
source: One of the strongest examples is atg13, which is incapable of performing autophagy (Funakoshi et al., 1997).
evidence: Statement about gene function supported by citation

claim: atg13 shows a strong reduction in the accumulation of the nucleoside inosine under rapamycin treatment.
source: This mutant shows a strong reduction in the accumulation of the nucleoside inosine under rapamycin treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Experimental observation with reference to figure

claim: The proteomes of six mutants in known positive regulators of TORC1 signaling and six receptor-related mutants were analyzed.
source: We tested this by analyzing the proteomes of six mutants in known positive regulators of TORC1 signaling, and the six receptor-related mutants that were associated with positive regulation of TORC1 signaling as was described above (Figure 2E).
evidence: Description of experimental approach with reference to figure

claim: Treatment of wild-type yeast with rapamycin resulted in broad changes in the proteome.
source: Treatment of wild-type yeast with rapamycin resulted in broad changes in the proteome, with enriched changes in the levels of proteins in gene ontology (GO) biological process categories such as carbohydrate and organic acid metabolism (Figure 3A), recapitulating patterns observed in previously published work (Iesmantavicius et al., 2014).
evidence: Experimental observation with reference to figure and citation

claim: All mutants except HXK2 and RGT2 showed clearly altered patterns of GO enrichment upon rapamycin treatment.
source: All mutants, except HXK2 and RGT2, showed clearly altered patterns of GO enrichment upon rapamycin treatment (Figure 3A), as would be expected for genes that are required to respond to rapamycin.
evidence: Observation from analysis with reference to figure

claim: BCK1, CLA4, and CFF1 showed similar proteomic profiles to known positive regulators of TOR signaling.
source: In addition to an altered proteome response to rapamycin, BCK1, CLA4, and CFF1 also showed similar proteomic profiles to known positive regulators of TOR signaling (Figure 3B).
evidence: Observation from analysis with reference to figure

claim: cff1 and bck1 showed the strongest correlations with rapamycin treatment.
source: All tested mutants showed a positive correlation in their proteome compared with that of wild-type treated with rapamycin, but cff1 and bck1 showed the strongest correlations with rapamycin treatment.
evidence: Observation from correlation analysis

claim: TORC1 signaling is central to the adaptation of the yeast cell to changing nutritional environments.
source: TORC1 signaling is central to the adaptation of the yeast cell to changing nutritional environments.
evidence: Statement about TORC1 function

claim: Mutations that impair TORC1 signaling reduce the ability of the cell to adapt to increases or decreases in nutritional quality.
source: Therefore, mutations that impair TORC1 signaling reduce the ability of the cell to adapt to increases or decreases in nutritional quality (Kira et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement about mutation effects supported by citation

claim: cff1 and bck1 showed significantly reduced growth rates upon supplementation of media with ammonium sulfate.
source: cff1 and bck1 showed significantly reduced growth rates upon the supplementation of the media with ammonium sulfate (Figure 3C), and hxk2 demonstrated a longer lag time (Figure 3D).
evidence: Experimental observation with reference to figures

claim: hxk2 demonstrated a longer lag time upon supplementation of media with ammonium sulfate.
source: cff1 and bck1 showed significantly reduced growth rates upon the supplementation of the media with ammonium sulfate (Figure 3C), and hxk2 demonstrated a longer lag time (Figure 3D).
evidence: Experimental observation with reference to figure

claim: Known positive regulators of TORC1 signaling show reduced growth rates when grown in minimal media compared with wild-type.
source: Previously published functional genomics screens have shown that known positive regulators of TORC1 signaling show reduced growth rates when grown in minimal media compared with wild-type (Breslow et al., 2008).
evidence: Statement about prior findings supported by citation

claim: SCH9 is directly phosphorylated by TORC1 and is a key node for transmission of signaling into processes downstream of TORC1.
source: The protein SCH9 is directly phosphorylated by TORC1 and is a key node for transmission of signaling intro processes downstream of TORC1 (Urban et al., 2007).
evidence: Statement about protein function supported by citation

claim: Western blot quantification revealed a similar degree of SCH9 phosphorylation in wild-type and cff1 strains in rich conditions.
source: As expected, Western blot quantification revealed a similar degree of SCH9 phosphorylation in wild-type and cff1 strains in rich conditions (Figure 4A).
evidence: Experimental observation with reference to figure

claim: The relative abundance of the CFF1 protein was reduced upon treatment with rapamycin.
source: Consistent with this expectation, the relative abundance of the CFF1 protein was reduced upon treatment rapamycin (Figure 4B).
evidence: Experimental observation with reference to figure

claim: Pyrimidine biosynthetic precursors (carbamoyl aspartate and dihydroorotate) were increased in cff1 compared with wild-type during nitrogen downshift.
source: LC-MS analysis of the samples indicated that pyrimidine biosynthetic precursors (carbamoyl aspartate and dihydroorotate) were increased in cff1 compared with wild-type (Figure 4C).
evidence: Experimental observation with reference to figure

claim: TOR signaling has been shown to stimulate de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis in other systems.
source: TOR signaling has been shown to stimulate de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis in other systems (Ben-Sahra et al., 2013; Robitaille et al., 2013), so the observation that CFF1 is required for the maintenance of pyrimidine precursor pool sizes during this nitrogen source shift further implicates its TORC1-related metabolic processes.
evidence: Statement about TOR function in other systems supported by citations

claim: The enzyme URA10 showed a significant decrease in abundance in cff1 mutant.
source: The enzyme URA10, which converts orotate into oratidine-5-phosphate (Figure 4D), showed a significant decrease in abundance (Figure 4E), which was not shared by the other members of the metabolic pathway (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Experimental observation with reference to figures

claim: CFF1 is required for normal adaptation of the cell to changing metabolic environments in terms of both up- and downshifts.
source: Taken together with earlier results, CFF1 is required for normal adaptation of the cell to changing metabolic environments in terms of both up- and downshifts with a specific role in the regulation of pyrimidine biosynthesis through URA10.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations

claim: This is the first demonstration that dynamic perturbation of the cell improves the recovery of eukaryotic gene function when using a metabolomics-based guilt-by-association scheme.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that dynamic perturbation of the cell improves the recovery of eukaryotic gene function when using a metabolomics-based guilt-by-association scheme.
evidence: Statement of novelty based on authors' knowledge

claim: CFF1 has structural similarity to auxin-binding proteins from plants.
source: Previous work has also demonstrated structural similarity between CFF1 and auxin-binding proteins from plants (Zhou et al., 2005), as well as a role in determining the production of the compound 4-hydroxymethylfuranone (Valastyan et al., 2021).
evidence: Statement about protein structure supported by citation

claim: CFF1 has a role in determining the production of the compound 4-hydroxymethylfuranone.
source: Previous work has also demonstrated structural similarity between CFF1 and auxin-binding proteins from plants (Zhou et al., 2005), as well as a role in determining the production of the compound 4-hydroxymethylfuranone (Valastyan et al., 2021).
evidence: Statement about gene function supported by citation

claim: CFF1 has been reported to be phosphorylated at a number of positions, including serine 68 under glucose limitation.
source: Intriguingly, CFF1 has been reported to be phosphorylated at a number of positions, including serine 68 under glucose limitation (Lanz et al., 2021).

claim: An interactive data visualization app was assembled where users can browse through the data.
source: To enhance the usability of this data, we assembled an interactive data visualization app where users can browse through this data in order to investigate mutants that are of interest to them (https://rapamycin-yeast.ethz.ch).

claim: The data are made available in raw form.
source: Furthermore, our data are made available in raw form, and because the acquisition of the main dataset was performed in an untargeted mode, these data can be reanalyzed in the future as the library of potential metabolites is expanded.

source: Furthermore, our data are made available in raw form, and because the acquisition of the main dataset was performed in an untargeted mode, these data can be reanalyzed in the future as the library of potential metabolites is expanded.

claim: Dynamic perturbations of gene expression can be used to recover drug-target relationships on the basis of metabolome similarity.
source: This builds on work showing that dynamic perturbations of gene expression can be used to recover drug-target relationships on the basis of metabolome similarity (Holbrook-Smith et al., 2022; Anglada-Girotto et al., 2022) and thus further demonstrates the value of non-steady-state perturbations of the cell in the context of metabolome profiling.
evidence: Statement about prior work supported by citations
